scope: src/main.js lines 32600-34950 — split-screen 2nd player, duel mode, endless waves, powerups, kill kick, player flags, tutorial hints, objective/radar/compass/footsteps ticks, aim assist, gamepad, story director.

findings.title: Endless mode fires a phantom 'WAVE 0' reward and double-schedules the first wave
findings.description: startEndlessMode() sets ENDLESS.active=true and G.started=true immediately (lines 32913,32919) but only schedules the first wave via setTimeout(endlessNextWave,2200) (line 32949). tickEndless() runs every frame once ENDLESS.active && G.started, and its transition guard is `if(alive===0 && !ENDLESS._waveTransition)` (line 33005). ENDLESS.wave is still 0 and _waveTransition is undefined on the very first frame, so before the 2200ms timeout fires, tickEndless immediately triggers a wave-transition: it awards money (`moneyPopup(200,'WAVE 0')`), grants a free heal pack, and schedules a SECOND endlessNextWave at +3500ms. Net result: a spurious 'WAVE 0' reward popup + free heal pack at the start, and two queued endlessNextWave calls so the player effectively skips from wave 1 to wave 2 within seconds.
findings.evidence: ENDLESS.active=true;ENDLESS.wave=0; ... setTimeout(()=>endlessNextWave(),2200);  // then in tickEndless: if(alive===0&&!ENDLESS._waveTransition){ENDLESS._waveTransition=true; const bonus=200+ENDLESS.wave*100; P.money+=bonus;moneyPopup(bonus,'WAVE '+ENDLESS.wave); P.healPacks=(P.healPacks||0)+1; ... setTimeout(()=>{ENDLESS._waveTransition=false;endlessNextWave();},3500);}
findings.fix: Guard the transition on a started wave: change line 33005 to `if(alive===0 && ENDLESS.wave>0 && !ENDLESS._waveTransition){`. (Alternatively set ENDLESS._waveTransition=true in startEndlessMode and clear it inside the first endlessNextWave.) The `ENDLESS.wave>0` guard is the smallest surgical fix and prevents the phantom WAVE 0 reward and the double-schedule.
findings.risk: Very low. Only changes behavior on the first frame(s) before wave 1 spawns; normal wave clears (wave>=1) are unaffected. No save-compat impact.

findings.title: spawnDmgNumber() wipes the #dmg-numbers container, erasing on-screen enemy barks on every hit
findings.description: spawnDmgNumber() was intentionally gutted (floating damage numbers are disabled by design, see comment at 26425-26426) but its body is `const c=$e('dmg-numbers'); if(c)c.innerHTML='';`. The SAME #dmg-numbers DOM container is reused by the enemy-bark renderer (line 32487 appends `.dmg-num` bark/voice-line elements into #dmg-numbers, removed via a 1100ms timeout). spawnDmgNumber is called on essentially every player hit (lines 25230, 25555, 26549). So each time the player lands a shot, c.innerHTML='' nukes any enemy bark text that is currently displayed, cutting bark lines short the instant combat starts — exactly when barks are most likely to be on screen.
findings.evidence: function spawnDmgNumber(worldPos,amt,isHead,killed,labelExtra){ const c=$e('dmg-numbers'); if(c)c.innerHTML=''; }   // and bark renderer: const c=$e('dmg-numbers');if(!c)return; ... el.className='dmg-num'; c.appendChild(el);
findings.fix: Make spawnDmgNumber a true no-op: delete the `if(c)c.innerHTML='';` lines so the function does nothing (the comment at 26425 already states damage numbers are intentionally off). The container is cleaned of stale damage numbers naturally; barks self-remove via their own timeout. If a hard reset is ever wanted, only remove children with class 'dmg-num' that are NOT barks, but the simplest correct fix is an empty body.
findings.risk: Very low. Removes an unintended side effect; floating damage numbers remain disabled as intended.

findings.title: AGILITY powerup (fastReload) has zero effect — never read as a powerup
findings.description: POWERUP_DEFS includes {id:'fastReload',name:'AGILITY',desc:'+100% reload speed · 15s'}. _grantPowerup pushes {id:'fastReload'} onto POWERUPS.active and shows a toast. But reload speed only ever consults the PERK system: `const reloadMul=hasPerk('fastReload')?.70:1.0;` (lines 27056,27089). Nothing calls hasActivePowerup('fastReload'). The powerup is fully spawnable (spawnPowerupPickup picks a random def) and grants a buff that is never read, so picking up AGILITY does nothing but flash a toast and advertise '+100% reload speed'.
findings.evidence: {id:'fastReload',name:'AGILITY',desc:'+100% reload speed · 15s',dur:15,col:0x40ff80}  // reload only checks: const reloadMul=hasPerk('fastReload')?.70:1.0;  (no hasActivePowerup('fastReload') anywhere)
findings.fix: In the reload-duration computation (lines 27056 and 27089), multiply reloadMul by an additional factor when the powerup is active, e.g. `if(typeof hasActivePowerup==='function'&&hasActivePowerup('fastReload'))reloadMul*=0.5;` to deliver the advertised +100% reload speed. (Choose 0.5 for the buff to roughly match the '+100% speed' wording.)
findings.risk: Low. Only shortens reload while the temporary buff is active; does not touch perk path or save shape.

findings.title: DOUBLER powerup (doubleScore) has zero effect — never read anywhere
findings.description: POWERUP_DEFS includes {id:'doubleScore',name:'DOUBLER',desc:'×2 score chain · 12s'}. _grantPowerup pushes {id:'doubleScore'} onto POWERUPS.active, but a repo-wide search shows nothing reads hasActivePowerup('doubleScore') (or 'doubleScore' at all outside the def). The promised ×2 score/combo chain never applies, so DOUBLER is a no-op buff that only shows a toast.
findings.evidence: {id:'doubleScore',name:'DOUBLER',desc:'×2 score chain · 12s',dur:12,col:0xffd060}  // grep 'doubleScore' returns only the def line; no hasActivePowerup('doubleScore') consumer
findings.fix: Either (a) wire it: in the combo/score award path (e.g. comboKill / money award sites), multiply the granted score/combo credit by 2 when hasActivePowerup('doubleScore'), or (b) if scoring multiplier is out of scope, drop 'doubleScore' from POWERUP_DEFS so the player is not handed a dead buff. Minimal surgical option is (b).
findings.risk: Low. (b) removes a never-functioning option; (a) adds a multiplier only while buff active.

findings.title: Ammo-type penetration multiplier (pen) is computed but never applied
findings.description: AMMO_TYPES advertise penetration behavior ('Better through cover', 'breaks on cover') and getAmmoMul() returns {dmg,pen,falloff}. The shoot path uses _ammoMul.falloff (line 26410) and _ammoMul.dmg (line 26417) but never uses _ammoMul.pen. So Armor-Piercing's 1.6× penetration and Hollow-Point's 0.4× penetration descriptions are unfulfilled — the only real differences between ammo types are raw damage and falloff. The headline 'through cover' promise is dead.
findings.evidence: pen:t?t.penetrationMul:1.0,  // in getAmmoMul; but only _ammoMul.falloff and _ammoMul.dmg are read in the firing code (26410,26417); grep for _ammoMul.pen / penetrationMul application returns nothing.
findings.fix: If wallbang/penetration logic exists for the weapon's through-cover damage, multiply that penetration strength (or post-penetration damage retention) by _ammoMul.pen at the penetration site. If penetration is out of scope, soften the AMMO_TYPES descriptions so they don't advertise unimplemented cover behavior. Low priority since dmg/falloff differences still make ammo types meaningful.
findings.risk: Low. Either a small multiply at the penetration site or a copy-only desc edit.

findings.title: _collectGamepads is a dead duplicate of _gatherPadsOrdered
findings.description: _collectGamepads (32635) and _gatherPadsOrdered (34143) are byte-for-byte the same logic (enumerate navigator.getGamepads(), keep connected pads, sort by index). _gatherPadsOrdered is the one wired into tickGamepad (34281). _collectGamepads is defined but never called anywhere (grep confirms only its own definition line).
findings.evidence: function _collectGamepads(){ ... out.sort((a,b)=>(a.index||0)-(b.index||0)); return out;}  // vs function _gatherPadsOrdered(){ ... out.sort((a,b)=>(a.index|0)-(b.index|0));return out;} — only _gatherPadsOrdered() is called (line 34281).
findings.fix: Delete _collectGamepads (lines 32635-32645). No callers, purely dead. Keeps the build green and removes a divergent copy that could drift from the real implementation.
findings.risk: Negligible. No references; removal cannot affect runtime.

findings.title: Radar enemy plotting computes rx_/rz_/ratio that are never used
findings.description: In tickRadar enemy loop, rx_ and rz_ are computed (rotation by +P.yaw) and then immediately discarded; the actual plotting recomputes lx/lz with rotation by -P.yaw (which is the correct orientation, verified: enemy directly ahead plots above center for both yaw=0 and yaw=PI). `ratio=d/RADAR_RANGE` is also computed but never used. The interleaved comments (34854-34860) are stale/confused leftovers from iterating on the orientation math.
findings.evidence: const rx_=Math.cos(ry)*dx+Math.sin(ry)*dz; const rz_=-Math.sin(ry)*dx+Math.cos(ry)*dz; // never used; const ratio=d/RADAR_RANGE; // never used; const px=cx+(lx/RADAR_RANGE)*RADAR_R; const py=cy+(lz/RADAR_RANGE)*RADAR_R;
findings.fix: Remove the dead `ry`, `rx_`, `rz_`, and `ratio` lines and the stale comment block; keep only the `ang=-P.yaw` / lx / lz / px / py computation. Pure cleanup — the visible radar output is unchanged.
findings.risk: Negligible. Removing unused locals; verified orientation math relies only on lx/lz.

findings.title: Gamepad dpad-left/right sets lean and also switches weapon when ADS+LB held
findings.description: When adsHeld is true, btn[14]/btn[15] (dpad L/R) set GAMEPAD._gpLeanLeft/_gpLeanRight (34193-34201). Separately, `if(slot===0&&lbHeld&&pressed(14))switchWeapon(prev)` (34243) fires regardless of adsHeld. So holding ADS + LB and tapping dpad-left both peeks (lean) AND cycles to the previous weapon in the same input, which is conflicting/unintended. The smoke/flash branch is correctly guarded with `&&!adsHeld`, but the LB weapon-cycle branch is not guarded against the lean state.
findings.fix: Add `&&!adsHeld` to the LB+dpad weapon-cycle conditions (lines 34243 and 34248), e.g. `if(slot===0&&lbHeld&&!adsHeld&&pressed(14))`, so peeking while ADS does not also swap weapons. This matches the existing guard pattern used for smoke/flash.
findings.risk: Low. Only changes gamepad binding behavior when ADS+LB are simultaneously held; preserves all other bindings.

findings.title: Duel keeps accepting damage/scoring after a winner is decided
findings.description: When DUEL.scores[scorer] reaches winTarget, DUEL.winner is set and quitToMain() is scheduled at +2600ms. But duelApplyDamage has no guard for `DUEL.winner>=0`, so for the 2.6s before quit both players can keep dealing damage and scoring further points (clamped by Math.min so no overflow, but extra 'POINT' toasts and respawn timers fire on top of the win banner). Reads as a minor polish bug: the win moment is cluttered by continued scoring.
findings.evidence: if(DUEL.scores[scorer]>=DUEL.winTarget){DUEL.winner=scorer; ... setTimeout(()=>quitToMain(),2600);}  // no early-out on DUEL.winner>=0 at top of duelApplyDamage
findings.fix: At the top of duelApplyDamage add `if(DUEL.winner>=0)return;` (after the playMode/active check) so no further damage/score is processed once the match is decided.
findings.risk: Very low. Only affects the post-win window; clamping already prevents score overflow.

findings.title: Endless reuses boss-bar but never resets boss-name/phase styling, and depends on the phantom-wave bug
findings.description: endlessNextWave repurposes #boss-name/#boss-fill/#boss-phase/#boss-bar to show wave info. Combined with the endless-phantom-wave0-reward bug, the first thing the player can see is the boss bar populated for 'WAVE 0' before wave 1 spawns. Independent of that bug, the boss bar is shown with `boss-bar.classList.add('show')` but there is no corresponding hide when endless mode ends/quits in this function's vicinity, and the bar retains boss-specific CSS classes if a real boss was previously fought in the same session before starting endless.
findings.fix: Primary fix is the endless-phantom-wave0-reward guard (ENDLESS.wave>0). Additionally ensure the boss-bar is hidden on endless exit (quitToMain/restart already clear ENDLESS.active at 38366/38535 — add `$e('boss-bar')?.classList.remove('show')` there if not already handled), and strip any boss-only modifier classes before reusing the bar for waves.
findings.risk: Low. HUD-only; verify the boss-bar hide path on quit isn't duplicated.
